eva_sales: Hi team — POC with ACME is failing during inference calls. Customer sees 401 / invalid_api_key plus occasional 404 project_not_found. Started during a key rotation this morning. Can we swarm?

sam_se: Ack. Can you paste the exact error body and the curl you used? Also which project id were they calling?

acme-dev: Here's the curl we ran (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  -d '{\"project_id\":\"proj-47b\",\"model\":\"rw-gpt-7b\",\"input\":\"hi\"}'
```
Response: 
```json
{\"error\":\"invalid_api_key\",\"message\":\"API key not valid for requested organization\"}
```

matt_eng: That exact message usually means the key is valid but not scoped to the org that owns proj-47b. There are two common root causes: (1) key belongs to a different org, (2) key lacks the project scope.

laura_support: Also check if the SDK or env is sending a header override. We saw cases where REDWOOD_ORG env var was unset and SDK defaulted to the org of the old key, causing mismatch.

sam_se: Can you run a quick inspect on the key? If you can't share the key here, run locally: `rdw keys inspect sk-prod-REDACTED` — it'll print the org_id and scopes. Example output: `org: org-12, scopes: [inference:invoke, project:read]`

acme-dev: Ran inspect — shows `org: org-9`, scopes `[inference:invoke]`. Their project proj-47b belongs to org-12. So that's probably it.

matt_eng: Yep — key org != project org. Two fixes: (A) mint a key scoped to org-12/project proj-47b, or (B) call a project under org-9. For POC I'd recommend a short-lived project-scoped key.

laura_support: Quick steps for the customer: (1) Create a project-key in Console > Projects > proj-47b > API Keys > New key, give it `inference:invoke` and `project:read` scopes. (2) Use header `Authorization: Bearer <key>` and include `X-Redwood-Project: proj-47b` only if your integration requires it. Most SDKs take project_id in the body.

sam_se: If they can't use console, you can create via API (needs admin token). Example curl (admins only):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/keys \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer admin-REDACTED\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  -d '{\"project_id\":\"proj-47b\",\"scopes\":[\"inference:invoke\",\"project:read\"],\"ttl_seconds\":3600}'
```

oncall-bot: request_id=rx-9c3 created for trace.

acme-dev: Created a project key with `inference:invoke, project:read`. Re-ran curl with new key and got 200. Output: `{ "request_id": "rx-9c3", "status": "ok", "output": "Hello\n" }`

eva_sales: Amazing — thanks everyone. Two followups: (1) can we add a small KB note to the POC checklist about org mismatch + how to inspect keys? (2) Sam/Matt — can we scope a one-click script for sales to mint POC keys for customers who give auth?

sam_se: Yes to both. I'll add a short KB and prototype a CLI helper: `rdw mint-poc-key --project proj-47b --scopes inference:invoke,project:read --ttl 3600`. Will run by security.

matt_eng: Happy to review the CLI. Also adding a validation in the SDK to warn when key org != project org would reduce confusion. Filing a tiny infra ticket.

laura_support: Marking resolved in the ticket for ACME. If anything else pops up ping me. :thumbsup:

acme-dev: Confirmed working end-to-end. Thanks for the quick help!

(threads ends)
